(a) The first sentence of section 409(a) (21 U.S.C. 1176(a)) is amended (1) by striking out “and” after “1978,”, and (2) by inserting after “1979,” the following: “September 30, 1980, and September 30, 1981,”. 
    (b) Section 409(e) is amended—

        (1) 
by inserting “(including women and the elderly)” after “population groups” in paragraph (3);
 
        (2) 
by amending paragraph (4) to read as follows:


“(4) 
describe the drug abuse prevention functions to be carried out under the plan with assistance under this section, set forth in detail the changes in emphasis among such functions resulting from shifts in demographic and drug abuse patterns within the State, and describe all other drug abuse prevention functions to be carried out within the State with assistance under this Act;”;

 
        (3) 
by inserting “, by the elderly,” after “by women” in clause (B) of paragraph (5), by striking out “and (B)” in paragraph (5) and inserting in lieu thereof “(B)”, and by inserting before the semicolon at the end of paragraph (5) the following: “; and (C) provide assurances satisfactory to the Secretary that, insofar as practicable, the survey conducted pursuant to clause (A) is coordinated with and not duplicative of the alcohol abuse and alcoholism survey conducted pursuant to section 303 of the Comprehensive Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism Prevention, Treatment, and Rehabilitation Act of 1970”;
 
        (4) 
by inserting “(A)” after “in the State” in paragraph (7) and by inserting before the semicolon in paragraph (7) the following: “, (B) to review and comment on the plan prior to its submission to the Secretary, and (C) to submit to the Secretary as an appendix to the plan such comments as such political subdivisions believe are relevant to approval of the plan under subsection (f)”;
 
        (5) 
by inserting “and to the extent feasible a survey of the extent to which other State programs and political subdivisions throughout the State are dealing effectively with the problems related to drug abuse and drug dependence,” after “under the plan,” in paragraph (10); and
 
        (6) 
by striking out “and” at the end of paragraph (12), by redesignating paragraph (13) as paragraph (17), and by inserting after paragraph (12) the following new paragraphs:


“(13) 
contain, to the extent feasible, a complete inventory of all public and private resources available in the State for the purpose of drug abuse and drug dependence treatment, prevention, and rehabilitation, including programs funded under State and local laws, occupational programs, voluntary organizations, education programs, military and Veterans’ Administration resources, and available public and private third-party payment plans;


“(14) 
provide assurance that the State agency will coordinate its planning with local drug abuse planning agencies, with State and local alcoholism and alcohol abuse planning agencies, and with other State and local health planning agencies;


“(15) 
provide assurance that the State agency—

“(A) 
will foster and encourage the development of drug abuse and drug dependence prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation programs and services in State and local governments and in private businesses and industry;


“(B) 
will make available to all business concerns and governmental entities within such State information and materials concerning such model programs suitable for replication on a cost-effective basis as are developed pursuant to section 413(b)(2) of this Act; and


“(C) 
will furnish technical assistance as feasible to such business concerns and governmental entities;



“(16) 
include a needs assessment of the severity of drug abuse problems within urban and nonurban areas of the State, an accounting of the existing and proposed allocation of resources among such areas, and a description of the role of units of general purpose local government in planning and coordinating the use of such resources; and”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this only amends state-plan requirements for a grant program, where coordination happens among state and local agencies and never reaches a federal decision. But the amended paragraph (7) lets political subdivisions (local governments, outside the federal government) submit comments directly to the Secretary that bear on the Secretary's decision to approve the plan. That is outside-party input into a federal decision, not merely intra-state coordination or a grant application, though the grant context makes this a close call.
fable.s: (C) to submit to the Secretary as an appendix to the plan such comments as such political subdivisions believe are relevant to approval of the plan under subsection (f)

opus.w: Political subdivisions (local governments, which are outside the federal government) may submit their own comments to the Secretary that are relevant to the Secretary's decision to approve the state plan under subsection (f). That is outside input into a federal approval decision. The tempting reading treats this as part of a grant application or as consultation inside the state, as in Example 9. But here the comments go directly to the federal decision-maker on the approval question.
opus.s: (B) to review and comment on the plan prior to its submission to the Secretary, and (C) to submit to the Secretary as an appendix to the plan such comments as such political subdivisions believe are relevant to approval of the plan under subsection (f)
opus.b:
I labelled this **Yes**, with moderate confidence (0.62).

**The tempting "No" reading:** This section amends what a state's plan for federal drug abuse grants must contain. Example 9 says consultation on a plan that a state submits to an agency is not participation. The definition also excludes applications for grants. Most of the section fits that pattern: the state agency coordinating with local planning agencies is all internal to the state's own planning.

**Why it fails here:** Amended paragraph (7) goes further. Local governments ("political subdivisions") may send their own comments directly to the Secretary, and those comments are expressly tied to the Secretary's decision whether to approve the plan under subsection (f). That gives outside parties a formal comment channel into a federal approval decision. It is not just the state applying for money, and it is not consultation kept inside the state. Local governments are outside the federal government, so the comments cross the federal boundary.

**Remaining doubt:** The decision being commented on is still approval of what is essentially a grant plan, so a reader could treat the whole thing as part of an application and answer "No."

qwen_chat.w: This section requires local political subdivisions to review and comment on a State plan before the State submits it to the Secretary. The consultation occurs between the State and local entities, not between the federal government and outside parties. The federal government (Secretary) receives the plan but is not required to consult with the local subdivisions or other outsiders before making a decision. Therefore, the federal government is not participating with outsiders.
qwen_chat.s: (4) by inserting “(A)” after “in the State” in paragraph (7) and by inserting before the semicolon in paragraph (7) the following: “, (B) to review and comment on the plan prior to its submission to the Secretary, and (C) to submit to the Secretary as an appendix to the plan such comments as such political subdivisions believe are relevant to approval of the plan under subsection (f)”;
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it requires local political subdivisions to "review and comment on the plan" before it is submitted to the Secretary.
Resolution: The plan being reviewed is a State plan, not a federal decision. The local governments are participating in the State's internal planning process, not in a federal decision-making process. The definition requires participation in a *federal* decision. Here, the State is making a decision (submitting a plan), and the locals are commenting on that State decision. The federal government (Secretary) only receives the final plan. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders before making a decision; the consultation is between state/local entities.

Wait, let's re-read carefully.
"provide assurances satisfactory to the Secretary that... the survey... is coordinated with..."
"to review and comment on the plan prior to its submission to the Secretary"
"submit to the Secretary as an appendix to the plan such comments"

The Secretary approves the State plan. Does the Secretary consult with anyone? No. The State consults with locals.
Is the State plan a "federal decision"? No, it's a state plan submitted for federal approval.
Does the section require the *federal government* to consult with outsiders? No.
Does it require outsiders to participate in a *federal* decision?
The definition says: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision."
Here, the *State* consults with locals. The *Federal Government* (Secretary) receives the plan. The Secretary does not consult with the locals. The Secretary consults with the State (which is outside the federal government, but the consultation is mandated by the State's plan requirements, not a direct federal consultation requirement in this text).
Actually, the text says the State plan must include assurances that it coordinated with locals. It doesn't say the Secretary must consult with locals.
Therefore, the federal government is not consulting with outsiders. The State is.
So the answer is No.

Let's double check if "State" is considered "outside the federal government". Yes.
But the *consultation* is not by the federal government. The federal government just receives the plan.
The definition: "Participation is when the **federal government** may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government..."
The actor doing the consulting here is the State agency, not the federal government.
So, No.
